record_type_quote: Our goal was to reproduce Waddington’s classic result confirming the “GA of an acquired adaptive character”, using our laboratory lines of D. melanogaster reared on three media with contrastingly different osmotic potential (high, intermediate, and low) for eight years (approximately 160 generations).

targets.title: Canalization of development and genetic assimilation of acquired characters.
targets.evidence_quote: Our goal was to reproduce Waddington’s classic result confirming the “GA of an acquired adaptive character”, using our laboratory lines of D. melanogaster reared on three media with contrastingly different osmotic potential (high, intermediate, and low) for eight years (approximately 160 generations).
targets.outcome_quote: We failed to replicate the genetic assimilation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report failure of genetic assimilation.

reasoning: Independent fly lines re-test Waddington’s published genetic-assimilation finding. The introduction explicitly attributes the anal-organ experiment to Waddington (1959); the abstract and discussion inconsistently cite 1953, whose separate reference concerns a different acquired character. Selected the 1959 entry tied specifically to the anal-organ experiment. Earlier replication attempts and ultrastructure sources supply comparisons/background rather than separately designated replication targets.
